exampleAnswers.title: Integrating a Trigonometric Expression Using the Tabular Method of Integration by Parts

question.explanation:
For this integral we choose $u = x^3+x$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = \cos(2x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
$\color[rgb]{1,0,0} x^3+x$ $ \cos(2x) $
$ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} 3x^2+1$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} \dfrac{\sin(2x)}{2}$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} + $ $\color[rgb]{1,0,0}\left(x^3+x\right)\dfrac{\sin(2x) }{2}$
$\color[rgb]{0,0,1} 6x $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} -\dfrac{\cos(2x)}{4}$ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} - $ $ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} (3x^2+1) \dfrac{\cos(2x)}{4} $
$\color[rgb]{1,0,1} 6 $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} -\dfrac{\sin(2x)}{8}$ $\color[rgb]{0,0,1} + $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} -\dfrac {3x \sin(2x)}{4} $
$0$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} \dfrac{\cos(2x)}{16}$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} -$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} -\dfrac {3\cos(2x)}{8} $

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. \begin{align} \int \left(x^3+x\right) \cos(2x)\, \textrm{d}x&= \left(x^3+x\right)\dfrac{\sin(2x) }{2} + (3x^2+1) \dfrac{\cos(2x)}{4}-\dfrac {3x \sin(2x)}{4} -\dfrac {3 \cos(2x)}{8}+ C\\[5pt] &= (2x^3- x)\dfrac{\sin(2x)}{4} + (6x^2- 1)\dfrac{\cos(2x)}{8} + C \end{align}

example.title: Integrating a Trigonometric Expression Using the Tabular Method of Integration by Parts

question.explanation:
For this integral we choose $u = 2x^4+4$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = \cos(3x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
$\color[rgb]{1,0,0}2x^4+4$ $ \cos(3x) $
$ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} 8x^3$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} \dfrac{\sin(3x)}{3}$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} + $ $\color[rgb]{1,0,0} \dfrac{(2x^4+4)\sin(3x)}{3} $
$\color[rgb]{0,0,1} 24x^2 $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} -\dfrac{\cos(3x)}{9}$ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06}- $ $ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} \dfrac{8x^3\cos(3x)}{9} $
$\color[rgb]{1,0,1} 48x $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} -\dfrac{\sin(3x)}{27}$ $\color[rgb]{0,0,1} + $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1}-\dfrac{8x^2\sin(3x)}{9}$
$ \color[rgb]{0,0.5,1} 48$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} \dfrac{\cos(3x)}{81}$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} -$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1}-\dfrac{16x\cos(3x)}{27} $
$0$ $\color[rgb]{0,0.5,1} \dfrac{\sin(3x)}{243}$ $\color[rgb]{0,0.5,1} +$ $\color[rgb]{0,0.5,1}\dfrac{16\sin(3x)}{81} $

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. \begin{align} \int (2x^4+4) \cos(3x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \dfrac{(2x^4+4)\sin(3x)}{3} +\dfrac{8x^3\cos(3x)}{9} -\dfrac{8x^2\sin(3x)}{9} -\dfrac{16x\cos(3x)}{27} + \dfrac{16\sin(3x)}{81} + C\\[5pt] &= \left(54x^4 - 72x^2 +124 \right)\dfrac{\sin(3x)}{81} + (24x^3-16x)\dfrac{\cos(3x)}{27}+ C \end{align}

question.explanation:
For this integral, we choose $u = 2x^3+3x^2+5$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = \sin(x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same Color Products
$\color[rgb]{1,0,0} 2x^3+3x^2+5$ $ \sin(x) $
$ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} 6x^2+6x$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} -\cos(x)$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} + $ $\color[rgb]{1,0,0} - (2x^3+3x^2+5)\cos(x) $
$\color[rgb]{0,0,1} 12x+6 $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} -\sin(x)$ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} - $ $ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} (6x^2+6x)\sin(x) $
$\color[rgb]{1,0,1} 12 $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} \cos(x) $ $\color[rgb]{0,0,1} + $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} (12x+6)\cos(x)$
$0$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} \sin(x)$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} -$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} -12\sin(x) $

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral. \begin{align} \int (2x^3+3x^2+5) \sin(x) \,\textrm{d}x &= -(2x^3+3x^2+5)\cos(x) + (6x^2+6x)\sin(x) \\[-3pt] &\phantom{=}\qquad\qquad\qquad + (12x+6)\cos(x) -12\sin(x) + C\\[5pt] &= -(2x^3+3x^2-12x -1)\cos(x) \\ &\phantom{=}\qquad\qquad\qquad + (6x^2+6x-12)\sin(x) + C \end{align}

question.explanation:
For this integral we choose $u =x^3+3x^2$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = \cos(2x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
$\color[rgb]{1,0,0} x^3+3x^2$ $ \cos(2x) $
$ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} 3x^2+6x$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} \dfrac{\sin(2x)}{2}$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} + $ $\color[rgb]{1,0,0} \dfrac{(x^3+3x^2 )\sin(2x)}{2} $
$\color[rgb]{0,0,1} 6x +6 $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} -\dfrac{\cos(2x)}{4}$ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} - $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} \dfrac{(3x^2+6x)\cos(2x)}{4} $
$\color[rgb]{1,0,1} 6 $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} -\dfrac{\sin(2x)}{8} $ $\color[rgb]{0,0,1} + $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} -\dfrac{(3x+3)\sin(2x)}{4}$
$0$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1}\dfrac{\cos(2x)}{16}$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} -$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} -\dfrac{3\cos(2x)}{8} $

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral.

\[\begin{align*} \int (x^3+3x^2) \cos(2x) \,\textrm{d}x &=\dfrac{(x^3+3x^2 )\sin(2x)}{2}+\dfrac{(3x^2+6x)\cos(2x)}{4} -\dfrac{(3x+3)\sin(2x)}{4} -\dfrac{3\cos(2x)}{8} + C\\[5pt] &=(2x^3+6x^2-3x-3)\dfrac{\sin(2x)}{4} + (6x^2+12x-3)\dfrac{\cos(2x)}{8} + C \end{align*}\]

question.explanation:
For this integral we choose $u = 2x^3$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = \sin(2x).$ Filling in the table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
$\color[rgb]{1,0,0} 2x^3$ $ \sin(2x) $
$ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} 6x^2$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} -\dfrac{\cos(2x)}{2}$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} + $ $\color[rgb]{1,0,0} -{x^3\cos(2x)}$
$\color[rgb]{0,0,1} 12x $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} -\dfrac{\sin(2x)}{4}$ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} - $ $ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} \dfrac{3x^2\sin(2x)}{2} $
$\color[rgb]{1,0,1} 12 $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} \dfrac{\cos(2x)}{8} $ $\color[rgb]{0,0,1} + $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} \dfrac{3x\cos(2x)}{2} $
$ 0$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} \dfrac{\sin(2x)}{16}$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} -$ $\color[rgb]{1,0,1} -\dfrac{3\sin(2x)}{4} $

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral.

\begin{align} \int 2x^3 \sin(2x) \, \textrm{d}x &= -{x^3\cos(2x)} + \dfrac{3x^2\sin(2x)}{2}+\dfrac{3x\cos(2x)}{2} -\dfrac{3\sin(2x)}{4} + C\\[5pt] &= (3x-2x^3)\dfrac{\cos(2x)}{2} + (6x^2-3)\dfrac{\sin(2x)}{4} + C \end{align}

question.explanation:
For this integral, we choose $u = 2x^3+3x^2+5$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = e^{2x}.$ Filling in our table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
$\color[rgb]{1,0,0} 2x^3+3x^2+5 $ $ e^{2x} $
$\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} 6x^2+6x $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0}\dfrac{e^{2x}}{2}$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} + $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0}\dfrac{(2x^3+3x^2+5)e^{2x}}{2} $
$\color[rgb]{0,0,1} 12x+6 $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} \dfrac{e^{2x}}{4} $ $ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06}- $ $ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} -\dfrac{(3x^2+3x)e^{2x}}{2} $
$\color[rgb]{1,0,1} 12 $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} \dfrac{e^{2x}}{8} $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} + $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} \dfrac{(6x+3)e^{2x}}{4} $
$0 $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,1} \dfrac{e^{2x}}{16} $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,1} - $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,1} -\dfrac{3e^{2x}}{4}$

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral.

\begin{align*} \int (2x^3+3x^2+5)e^{2x}\, \textrm{d}x& = \dfrac{e^{2x}}{4}\Big[2(2x^3+3x^2+5)-2(3x^2+3x)+(6x+3)-3\Big] + C \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{e^{2x}}{4}(4x^3+10) +C\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{e^{2x}}{2}(2x^3+5) +C \end{align*}

question.explanation:
For this integral, we choose $u = 2x^4$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = e^{4x}.$ Filling in our table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
$\color[rgb]{1,0,0} 2x^4 $ $ e^{4x} $
$\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} 8x^3 $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0}\dfrac{e^{4x}}{4}$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} + $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0}\dfrac{x^4e^{4x}}{2} $
$\color[rgb]{0,0,1} 24x^2 $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} \dfrac{e^{4x}}{16} $ $ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} - $ $ \color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} -\dfrac{x^3e^{4x}}{2}$
$\color[rgb]{1,0,1} 48x $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} \dfrac{e^{4x}}{64} $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} + $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} \dfrac{3x^2e^{4x}}{8}$
$\color[rgb]{0,0.5,1} 48 $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,1} \dfrac{e^{4x}}{256} $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,1} - $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,1} -\dfrac{3xe^{4x}}{16}$
$0 $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0.5,1}\dfrac{e^{4x}}{1024}$ $ \color[rgb]{0,0.5,1}+ $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0.5,1} \dfrac{3e^{4x}}{64}$

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral.

\[\int 2x^4e^{4x} \,\textrm{d}x = \dfrac{e^{4x}}{64}(32x^4-32x^3+24x^2-12x+3) + C\]

question.explanation:
For this integral, we choose $u = 2x^4+4x$ and $\dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}x} = e^{3x}.$ Filling in our table gives the following:

Derivatives Integrals Sign Same-color Products
$\color[rgb]{1,0,0} 2x^4+4x $ $ e^{3x} $
$\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} 8x^3 +4 $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0}\dfrac{e^{3x}}{3}$ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0} + $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,0}\dfrac{(2x^4+4x)e^{3x}}{3} $
$\color[rgb]{0,0,1} 24x^2 $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} \dfrac{e^{3x}}{9} $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} - $ $\color[rgb]{0.77,0.45,0.06} -\dfrac{(8x^3+4)e^{3x}}{9}$
$\color[rgb]{1,0,1} 48x $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} \dfrac{e^{3x}}{27} $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} + $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0,1} \dfrac{8x^2e^{3x}}{9}$
$\color[rgb]{0,0.5,1} 48 $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,1} \dfrac{e^{3x}}{81} $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,1} - $ $ \color[rgb]{1,0,1} -\dfrac{16xe^{3x}}{27}$
$0 $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0.5,1}\dfrac{e^{3x}}{243}$ $ \color[rgb]{0,0.5,1}+ $ $ \color[rgb]{0,0.5,1}\dfrac{16e^{3x}}{81}$

We add up all the terms of the last column to get the answer for our integral.

\[\begin{align*} \int (2x^4+4x)e^{3x} \,\textrm{d}x &= \dfrac{e^{3x}}{81}(27(2x^4+4x) -9(8x^3+4)+9(8x^2)-3(16x)+16) + C\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{e^{3x}}{81}(54x^4-72x^3+72x^2+60x-20)+C\\[3pt] &= \dfrac{2e^{3x}}{81}(27x^4-36x^3+36x^2+30x-10)+C \end{align*}\]
